title: a write verb's title positional absorbs a mistyped subcommand name and creates permanent state at rc=0 -- five artefacts of it are in this register
body:
A write verb's TITLE positional silently absorbs a mistyped subcommand or flag name and creates permanent project state at rc=0. **The register carries five artefacts of it, and they are why this was found.**

## Driven, in a throwaway `intent init` project, on 6dac00f7

    $ intent issues add help          -> rc=0   created: intent/.canon/issues/0001.json
    $ intent st new help              -> rc=0   created: ST0001
    $ intent issues add --help        -> rc=0   Add a new issue, print its ID:TITLE
    $ intent issues add               -> rc=1   error: the following required arguments were not provided: <TITLE>

Controls: `intent st show ST9999` -> rc=1 and `false` -> rc=1, so the instrument can see a non-zero. **An earlier run of this drive reported rc=0 for every line because it read `$?` after a pipe through `head`; the figures above are from the corrected instrument.**

So the two arms that should catch a mistake DO: `--help` prints help, and a missing positional refuses. **The gap is the bare word**, which is exactly what a user types.

## THE EVIDENCE IS IN THIS PROJECT'S OWN REGISTER

`9d717901` (2026-08-26) committed what was found uncommitted at the v3.0.0 cut. In that one batch:

    issue 0095   title "help"        body EMPTY
    issue 0096   title "severity"    body EMPTY
    ST0061       title "dehydrate"   objective EMPTY
    ST0062       title "help"        objective EMPTY
    ST0063       title "start"       objective EMPTY

**Five entities, one batch, every title an intent subcommand or flag name** -- `help`, `severity`, `dehydrate`, `start`. That is not somebody filing an issue titled `help`; it is somebody exploring the CLI and leaving debris in the project's permanent record. The commit's own message says they were touched at 10:48 local, before any session began, and claimed by no node.

## WHAT THIS IS NOT

**It is not that `help` should be refused as a title.** A title can legitimately be the word `help` -- an issue about the help system is a real issue. Refusing the string would be the wrong fix and would break a legitimate use.

**The defect is that a WRITE happens with no confirmation and no way back.** `0090` and `0151` mean an issue body and title are write-once, so a junk row created this way cannot be corrected or retitled; it can only be closed. Three of the five artefacts above are still open in the register today, and two of them (`0095`, `0096`) are undispositioned members of `AC-02.3`'s population -- they cost real work precisely because nothing can be recovered from them.

## FOUND BY

dc, 2026-09-03, while running hv's `AC-02.3` fixture-coverage census. `0095` and `0096` were the two members the census reported BLOCKED as undecidable. They are not undecidable -- they are artefacts, and this is what they are artefacts OF.

## ROOT CAUSE IS NOT ESTABLISHED AND IS DELIBERATELY NOT GUESSED

The observed behaviour is recorded above. Whether the right remedy is a confirmation on a bare bare-word title that collides with a known subcommand, a `--title` flag, or nothing at all is a design call this issue does not pre-empt.
